rubrics.title: Q3 Music & Identity Comparative Essay Rubric

Cultural and historical context: accurate, specific geographic and cultural overview; the tradition is placed in its history
Musical analysis: analysis of at least one named recording using at least 4 of the six elements correctly and specifically
Listening example: an appropriate excerpt is played within the presentation and discussed
Personal reflection: a genuine, specific reflection on what this tradition taught the student
Sources and citation: works-cited slide or sheet with at least 3 legitimate sources, cited consistently

questions.text: In the early 1970s the South Bronx was losing services, schools, and whole blocks of housing, and out of that neighborhood came the most influential music of the last fifty years. Why do you think powerful new art so often comes from places under pressure? Two or three sentences of your first instinct, no wrong answer.
This module I will:

answers.text: name and describe the four elements of hip-hop culture
explain how DJ Kool Herc's breakbeat technique and the sample turned the turntable into an instrument
trace the MC's evolution from party hype to social documentary and name key golden age artists

questions.text: Before we start: how confident are you that you could explain what makes hip-hop a culture rather than just a music genre?

answers.text: 1 - Not confident
3 - Somewhat confident
5 - Very confident

questions.text: At the start of this module you guessed why powerful art comes from places under pressure. Now that you know the story of the South Bronx, the four elements, and the golden age, how would you answer that question differently?
Match each term to its one-line definition.

answers.right: A culture born in the South Bronx with four elements: DJing, MCing, breaking, and graffiti writing
The DJ who hosted the 1973 party at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue and extended the break with the merry-go-round technique
The short, drum-only section of a funk record that DJs isolate and extend for dancers
Lifting a fragment of an existing recording and looping it as raw material for a new track
Moving a record back and forth under the needle to make rhythmic, percussive sounds
The rapper or master of ceremonies who rhymes over the beat
The 1982 record by Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five that used rap to document social conditions in a neglected city

questions.text: In your own words, what is the difference between sampling and scratching?
A quiz is coming. Which of this module's vocabulary words is still fuzzy for you? Name it and write your best current definition.

This module I will:

answers.text: trace salsa from the Cuban son to New York City and explain what the clave does inside the ensemble

switching between two copies of the same record on two turntables, cueing each back to the start of the break

Where else have you watched something move from the margins to the center? What did it keep, and what did it change, on the way?
When an artist carries a centuries-old musical tradition into hip-hop or electronic music, is something being lost, gained, or both? Two or three sentences of your first instinct, no wrong answer.
This module I will:

answers.text: describe how contemporary Native artists blend traditional elements with hip-hop, electronic, and folk-rock forms
explain what makes this music an act of sovereignty and cultural revitalization
distinguish between music a tradition chooses to share and sacred material that is not for outside performance

answers.text: 1 - Not well

A sung syllable that carries musical and emotional meaning without being a word in the spoken language
Hip-hop made by Native artists, a new register for Native storytelling that can blend in traditional elements
A nation's right to govern itself and its culture
Actively bringing languages, songs, and practices forward into daily life rather than preserving them behind glass

Some ceremonial songs will never appear on streaming platforms, and the lesson says that is not a gap but a boundary. Describe one thing in your own life or community that is shared only with certain people, and why that boundary is worth respecting.
